overview: ResMed Inc. is a San Diego-based global leader in digital health and cloud-connected medical devices for the diagnosis, treatment, and management of sleep apnea, COPD, and other respiratory conditions. The company sells CPAP/APAP/bilevel devices, masks, and accessories (Sleep and Breathing Health segment, ~88% of FY2026 revenue) alongside cloud-based patient engagement software (AirView, myAir) and business-management SaaS for out-of-hospital care providers (Residential Care Software segment, Brightree and MEDIFOX DAN, ~12% of revenue, following the September 2026 sale of MatrixCare/HealthcareFirst/Citus Health). ResMed operates in more than 140 countries, with roughly 58% of FY2026 revenue from the Americas and the remainder from Europe, Asia, and other international markets.

business_model.summary: ResMed sells durable medical devices (CPAP/APAP/bilevel/ventilators) that generate an initial hardware sale followed by recurring, high-margin revenue from replacement masks, cushions, tubing, filters, and other consumables on a roughly 6-12 month replacement cycle, plus growing cloud software subscription/SaaS revenue (Brightree, MEDIFOX DAN) for home medical equipment and care providers. Device sales are driven by new diagnoses and device replacement (useful life ~5 years); masks/accessories are a recurring, almost annuity-like revenue stream tied to the installed base; SaaS revenue is subscription-based and recurring.

revenue_streams.name: Residential Care Software (SaaS)
revenue_streams.trend: growing, but segment shrinking post-MatrixCare divestiture

business_model.customer_type: Primarily B2B2C — sells through home medical equipment (HME) providers, durable medical equipment (DME) dealers, hospitals, and sleep clinics that serve individual patients; SaaS segment sells directly to home health, hospice, skilled nursing, and senior living providers (B2B/enterprise)
business_model.geographic_mix: Americas (U.S., Canada, Latin America) ~58%, Rest of World (Europe, Asia Pacific, other international) ~42% of FY2026 revenue

competitive_position.market_position: Dominant global leader in CPAP/sleep apnea devices with an estimated 55-60% share of the global CPAP device market, a position significantly strengthened since Philips' 2021 Respironics foam recall forced Philips to exit new device sales in the U.S. market (Philips has since resumed limited production and remains under an FDA consent decree). Fisher & Paykel Healthcare is the next-largest device competitor; Inspire Medical Systems competes with an implantable neurostimulation alternative to CPAP in moderate-to-severe OSA.

moat_factors.description: Tens of millions of patients on therapy generate a recurring, high-margin replacement stream for masks and accessories independent of new device sales

AirView/myAir platform connects millions of therapy devices, creating switching costs for both patients (compliance tracking, insurance reimbursement data) and HME providers who rely on remote monitoring workflows
Decades of FDA clearances and clinical data, reinforced by Philips' recall, make ResMed the default choice for physicians and DME providers
Scale in device and mask manufacturing supports industry-leading gross margins (~61% FY2026) versus smaller rivals
Brightree and MEDIFOX DAN are deeply embedded in HME/home-health billing and clinical workflows, creating stickiness, though this is a smaller and now-shrinking part of the business

weaknesses: High dependence on reimbursement policy and payer relationships (Medicare, private insurers) in the U.S.
Narrowing competitive tailwind as Philips works to re-enter the U.S. CPAP market following its recall-driven absence
Exposure to single-source suppliers for certain uniquely configured components
Residential Care Software segment is sub-scale relative to dedicated EHR/software competitors and now smaller after the MatrixCare divestiture
Device replacement cycle creates revenue lumpiness tied to macro/consumer discretionary spending and insurance deductible resets

growth_drivers: Large under-diagnosed/under-treated global sleep apnea population (estimated ~936 million adults with OSA worldwide) provides a long runway for new patient starts

GLP-1/anti-obesity drug adoption is proving to be a net tailwind rather than a threat: ResMed data on ~2.5 million linked patients shows GLP-1 users are more likely to initiate and stay compliant with CPAP therapy, and the company is running physician education programs to drive sleep apnea screening among GLP-1 patients
Continued share gains as Philips Respironics works through its FDA consent decree and slowly rebuilds U.S. device supply
New product cycle (AirSense 11, AirCurve 11, lighter/quieter masks, NightOwl home diagnostic) supporting device upgrades and new patient setups
International expansion in under-penetrated Asia-Pacific, Latin America, and European markets
Residential Care Software/SaaS growth (Brightree, MEDIFOX DAN) in HME billing and home-health/hospice workflows, now more focused after shedding MatrixCare
Capital return acceleration — FY2027 guidance of ~$1.5B buybacks (incl. accelerated share repurchase) plus a 10% dividend increase, totaling >$1.85B returned to shareholders
Gross margin expansion from manufacturing productivity, mix shift toward higher-margin masks/accessories, and selective price increases

business.description: ResMed cannot predict the timing or scale of Philips Respironics' return to full U.S. device sales as its consent decree is resolved; a well-capitalized competitor regaining share (potentially with discounting) could pressure both volumes and pricing
Medicare competitive bidding, prior authorization requirements, and private payer coverage changes can affect device/mask reimbursement rates and patient access

Revenue is heavily concentrated in sleep apnea/respiratory devices and consumables; a major product recall or quality issue (as Philips experienced) would be highly damaging given reliance on brand trust
Certain uniquely configured components are sourced from single suppliers; disruption could constrain manufacturing until a qualified replacement is found

financial.description: ~42% of revenue from outside the Americas creates translation and transaction FX exposure that has caused reported-vs-constant-currency growth gaps in recent quarters
The $490M MatrixCare sale to Frazier Healthcare Partners closed September 2026; integration/separation (TSAs, cost dis-synergies) carries modest near-term execution risk
FY2027 guidance of ~$1.5B in buybacks plus dividend increases is large relative to free cash flow (~$1.6-1.7B FY2026), though balance sheet leverage remains low (D/E ~0.13)

regulatory.description: Medical device products require ongoing FDA clearance/compliance; new product launches and manufacturing changes are subject to regulatory review and potential delay
Changes to U.S. healthcare reimbursement frameworks, tariff policy on medical devices, or international regulatory regimes (EU MDR, etc.) could raise compliance costs or affect pricing
Products treating chronic respiratory disease have historically been exempted from most tariff actions, limiting (but not eliminating) exposure to global trade tensions

macro.description: While current data shows GLP-1 drugs as a net positive for CPAP compliance, sustained, large-scale weight loss across the population could eventually reduce OSA prevalence/severity over the long term, a risk management says is currently limited but is watched closely by investors
High-deductible health plans and co-pays can delay device purchases or mask replacement, a modest cyclicality tied to consumer financial health
Company guidance explicitly flags ongoing macro uncertainty and inflation across electronic components and freight, partially offset by productivity and pricing

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global sleep apnea diagnosis and treatment market is in a long multi-decade growth phase due to low diagnosis rates (an estimated <20% of OSA sufferers are diagnosed), rising obesity-linked disease prevalence, and growing awareness; the home respiratory care and connected-health software markets are both expected to grow at high-single to low-double-digit rates over the medium term
macro_factors.cyclicality: Low to moderate — healthcare device demand is relatively defensive versus broad consumer discretionary spending, though device replacement timing and elective-care deductible dynamics introduce some mild cyclicality
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct sensitivity given a low-leverage balance sheet (D/E ~0.13, net cash position); indirect sensitivity through valuation multiple compression in a high-rate environment given the stock's growth/quality premium

recent_developments.event: Closed the sale of MatrixCare (and related HealthcareFirst/Citus Health home-health/hospice software) to Frazier Healthcare Partners for approximately $490 million, narrowing the Residential Care Software segment to Brightree (U.S.) and MEDIFOX DAN (Germany) to refocus capital and management attention on core sleep and breathing health

Reported record Q4 FY2026 revenue of ~$1.5 billion, up 9% reported / 8% constant currency; non-GAAP EPS up 16% to $2.95; full-year FY2026 revenue grew 10% reported / 8% constant currency with non-GAAP EPS growth of 17% and ~$1.6 billion of free cash flow

Issued FY2027 guidance of $5.75-5.85 billion revenue and non-GAAP EPS of $12.00-12.25 (+7-10%), with low-double-digit gross margin basis-point expansion expected, alongside a Q4 earnings call noting incremental headwinds from the Astral ventilator product line

Announced a 10% increase in the quarterly dividend to $0.66/share and a capital return plan of more than $1.85 billion for FY2027, including an accelerated share repurchase program (~$1.5 billion planned buybacks)

Continued to publish data (on a cohort of ~2.5 million linked patients) showing GLP-1 anti-obesity drug use is correlated with higher CPAP therapy initiation and higher resupply/compliance rates, positioning GLP-1 adoption as a tailwind rather than a disruptive threat to device demand

Philips Respironics remained under its U.S. FDA consent decree while slowly working to resume broader device production and distribution; the market continues to debate the timing and competitive impact of a fuller Philips re-entry into the U.S. CPAP market

items.notes: Implies ~2-3.5% reported growth off FY2026's $5.65B base; FY2026 constant-currency growth was 8%, so FY2027 guidance appears conservative/embeds currency and divestiture effects from the MatrixCare sale
Represents approximately 7-10% growth on a reported basis versus FY2026 non-GAAP EPS
Driven by productivity efficiencies and modest strategic price increases, partially offset by macro uncertainty and inflation in electronic components and freight
Consistent with continued opex discipline alongside gross margin gains

items.vs_prior: raised (>70% increase in FY2026 capital returns, further increased for FY2027)
items.notes: Includes ~$1.5 billion of share repurchases (inclusive of an accelerated share repurchase program) plus dividends after a 10% quarterly dividend increase to $0.66/share

guidance.management_commentary: Management described FY2026 as a strong year with record revenue and double-digit non-GAAP EPS growth, while flagging incremental headwinds from the Astral ventilator product line heading into FY2027. Leadership framed the MatrixCare divestiture as sharpening focus on the higher-growth, scalable sleep, breathing, and connected home-based care opportunity (part of a stated '2030 strategy'), and reiterated that GLP-1 drug adoption is being treated as a net positive for CPAP compliance and resupply rather than a structural demand risk.

bull_case: Dominant ~55-60% share of a large, structurally under-diagnosed global sleep apnea market with a multi-decade growth runway and recurring, high-margin mask/accessory revenue tied to a large and growing installed base

GLP-1 weight-loss drug adoption is emerging as a demand tailwind (higher CPAP initiation/compliance in linked-patient data) rather than the disruptive threat the market initially feared, removing a key overhang on the stock

Philips Respironics' multi-year absence from full-scale U.S. device sales (recall + consent decree) has structurally entrenched ResMed's market leadership, and even a gradual Philips re-entry leaves ResMed the dominant incumbent with superior scale, data platform, and brand trust

Strong and accelerating capital returns (>$1.85B planned for FY2027, including an accelerated buyback and a 10% dividend hike) on a low-leverage balance sheet (D/E ~0.13) support EPS growth and shareholder returns independent of top-line acceleration

Sharper strategic focus after shedding MatrixCare — management is concentrating capital and management attention on the core, higher-margin sleep/breathing health franchise and the remaining Brightree/MEDIFOX DAN SaaS businesses
bear_case: FY2027 reported revenue guidance of $5.75-5.85B implies a meaningful deceleration from FY2026's 8-10% growth, raising questions about whether device/mask volume growth is slowing as GLP-1 and macro effects play out

Philips Respironics could still stage a more aggressive U.S. re-entry with price discounting once its consent decree issues are fully resolved, pressuring ResMed's pricing and share in its most profitable market

Long-term disease-modifying effects of sustained, population-level GLP-1 weight loss on OSA prevalence remain uncertain, and the current favorable compliance data does not rule out a longer-run reduction in new-patient device demand
Astral ventilator product line headwinds flagged by management for FY2027 add a product-specific drag to an otherwise diversified device portfolio

Valuation reflects ResMed's quality/moat premium (consensus analyst rating is roughly a Hold with price targets clustered near current levels), leaving limited room for multiple expansion if growth continues to moderate
